bibl.title: Diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis: 2010 revisions to the McDonald criteria

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A DIAGNOSTIC DEFINITION ON ITS THIRD REVISION BY THE SAME PANEL, LOOSENED EACH TIME ON PURPOSE - the McDonald Criteria of 2001, revised 2005 and again here, each round making the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis earlier and the procedure simpler
span.quote: New evidence and consensus has led to further revision of the McDonald Criteria for diagnosis of multiple sclerosis. The use of imaging for demonstration of dissemination of central nervous system lesions in space and time has been simplified, and in some circumstances dissemination in space and time can be established by a single scan. These revisions simplify the Criteria, preserve their diagnostic sensitivity and specificity, address their applicability across populations, and may allow earlier diagnosis and more uniform and widespread use.

span.label: how far the imaging requirements for demonstrating dissemination in space and time can be simplified without losing specificity, and whether the criteria hold outside the population they were derived from
span.quote: Since the revision of the McDonald Criteria in 2005, new data and consensus have pointed to the need for their simplification to improve their comprehension and utility and for evaluating their appropriateness in populations that differ from the largely Western Caucasian adult populations from which the Criteria were derived. In May 2010 in Dublin, Ireland, the International Panel on Diagnosis of MS (the Panel) met for a third time to examine requirements for demonstrating DIS and DIT and to focus on application of the McDonald Criteria in pediatric, Asian, and Latin American populations.

span.label: MAGNIMS-based imaging criteria for dissemination in space, a rule letting enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on ONE scan establish dissemination in time, and recommendations for pediatric, Asian and Latin American populations
span.quote: By using the recommended simplified MAGNIMS criteria to demonstrate DIS 22 and allowing DIT to be demonstrated by a scan containing both enhancing and nonenhancing lesions in regions of the CNS typical for MS, 23 a diagnosis of MS can be made in some CIS patients based on a single MRI. The Panel felt this is justified because it simplifies the diagnostic process without reducing accuracy. However, a new clinical event or serial imaging to show a new enhancing or T2 lesion will still be required to establish DIT in those patients who do not have both gadolinium-enhancing and nonenhancing lesions on their baseline MRI.

span.label: method
span.quote: In its discussions, the Panel stressed that the McDonald Criteria should only be applied in those patients who present with a typical clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) suggestive of MS or symptoms consistent with a CNS inflammatory demyelinating disease, because the development and validation of the Criteria have been limited to patients with such presentations. CIS presentations can be monofocal or multifocal, and typically involve the optic nerve, brainstem/cerebellum, spinal cord, or cerebral hemispheres.

span.label: a disease with no confirmatory biomarker, diagnosed by a rule that has been rewritten three times, whose rewriting changes which past trial subjects would have qualified
span.quote: The Panel acknowledges that using these refined diagnostic criteria may change some of the outcomes of patients in natural history studies and clinical trials, when original expectations for outcomes may be based on subjects whose diagnosis was made using past, somewhat different criteria.

span.label: an international panel meeting for the third time, reviewing published research and adopting the MAGNIMS network's comparative studies of competing imaging criteria
span.term: an international panel meeting for the third time, reviewing published research and adopting the MAGNIMS network's comparative studies of competing imaging criteria
span.quote: Since the revision of the McDonald Criteria in 2005, new data and consensus have pointed to the need for their simplification to improve their comprehension and utility and for evaluating their appropriateness in populations that differ from the largely Western Caucasian adult populations from which the Criteria were derived. In May 2010 in Dublin, Ireland, the International Panel on Diagnosis of MS (the Panel) met for a third time to examine requirements for demonstrating DIS and DIT and to focus on application of the McDonald Criteria in pediatric, Asian, and Latin American populations.

span.label: **A DEFINITION DELIBERATELY LOOSENED, THREE TIMES, BY THE SAME PANEL**: `These revisions SIMPLIFY THE CRITERIA, PRESERVE THEIR DIAGNOSTIC SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY, address their applicability across populations, and MAY ALLOW EARLIER DIAGNOSIS and more uniform and widespread use.` The corpus holds definitions tightened, abolished and kept for continuity. **This one has been relaxed on purpose in 2001, 2005 and 2010, each time with the sensitivity/specificity claim attached**
span.quote: New evidence and consensus has led to further revision of the McDonald Criteria for diagnosis of multiple sclerosis. The use of imaging for demonstration of dissemination of central nervous system lesions in space and time has been simplified, and in some circumstances dissemination in space and time can be established by a single scan. These revisions simplify the Criteria, preserve their diagnostic sensitivity and specificity, address their applicability across populations, and may allow earlier diagnosis and more uniform and widespread use.

span.label: **AND DISSEMINATION IN TIME IS NOW DEMONSTRABLE AT A SINGLE MOMENT**: `in some circumstances DISSEMINATION IN SPACE AND TIME CAN BE ESTABLISHED BY A SINGLE SCAN` - because `a single brain MRI study that demonstrates DIS AND BOTH ASYMPTOMATIC GADOLINIUM-ENHANCING AND NON-ENHANCING LESIONS is highly specific for predicting early development of clinically definite MS`. **A criterion whose name is TIME, satisfied without the passage of any** - the two lesion types imply different ages, so one image carries a history
span.quote: By using the recommended simplified MAGNIMS criteria to demonstrate DIS 22 and allowing DIT to be demonstrated by a scan containing both enhancing and nonenhancing lesions in regions of the CNS typical for MS, 23 a diagnosis of MS can be made in some CIS patients based on a single MRI. The Panel felt this is justified because it simplifies the diagnostic process without reducing accuracy. However, a new clinical event or serial imaging to show a new enhancing or T2 lesion will still be required to establish DIT in those patients who do not have both gadolinium-enhancing and nonenhancing lesions on their baseline MRI.

span.label: AND A WAITING REQUIREMENT WAS DROPPED BECAUSE IT COST A SCAN: `The 2005 revision ... based [DIT] on the appearance of a new T2 lesion on a scan compared to a reference or baseline scan performed AT LEAST 30 DAYS AFTER THE ONSET ... In clinical practice, however, there is reason NOT TO POSTPONE A FIRST MRI until after 30 days, WHICH WOULD RESULT IN AN EXTRA MRI SCAN to confirm a diagnosis. ABANDONING THE REQUIREMENT ... DOES NOT COMPROMISE SPECIFICITY.` A criterion removed on cost, with the specificity claim cited beside it
span.quote: The 2005 revision of the McDonald Criteria simplified the MRI evidence required for DIT, basing it on the appearance of a new T2 lesion on a scan compared to a reference or baseline scan performed at least 30 days after the onset of the initial clinical event. In clinical practice, however, there is reason not to postpone a first MRI until after 30 days of clinical onset, which would result in an extra MRI scan to confirm a diagnosis. Abandoning the requirement for an extra reference MRI after 30 days does not compromise specificity, 28 and therefore the Panel, in its current revision of the McDonald Criteria, allows a new T2 lesion to establish DIT irrespective of the timing of the baseline MRI.

span.label: **AND A FURTHER LIBERALISATION WAS REFUSED, FOR A REASON ABOUT THE EVIDENCE BASE**: `In the 2001 and 2005 McDonald Criteria, A POSITIVE CSF FINDING COULD BE USED TO REDUCE THE MRI REQUIREMENTS ... However, when applying the simplified MAGNIMS imaging criteria, the Panel believes that EVEN FURTHER LIBERALIZING MRI REQUIREMENTS IN CSF-POSITIVE PATIENTS IS NOT APPROPRIATE, AS CSF STATUS WAS NOT EVALUATED FOR ITS CONTRIBUTION TO THE MAGNIMS CRITERIA.` **A relaxation declined because the variable was not in the study the new rule came from** - and an existing allowance withdrawn by the same reasoning
span.quote: In the 2001 and 2005 McDonald Criteria, a positive CSF finding could be used to reduce the MRI requirements for reaching DIS criteria (requiring only 2 or more MRI-detected lesions consistent with MS if the CSF was positive). 8 , 9 However, when applying the simplified MAGNIMS imaging criteria for DIS and DIT, 24 the Panel believes that even further liberalizing MRI requirements in CSF-positive patients is not appropriate, as CSF status was not evaluated for its contribution to the MAGNIMS criteria for DIS and DIT.

span.label: **AND THE PANEL SAYS THE REVISION CHANGES WHAT THE EARLIER TRIALS WERE ABOUT**: `The Panel acknowledges that USING THESE REFINED DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA MAY CHANGE SOME OF THE OUTCOMES OF PATIENTS IN NATURAL HISTORY STUDIES AND CLINICAL TRIALS, when original expectations for outcomes may be based on subjects WHOSE DIAGNOSIS WAS MADE USING PAST, SOMEWHAT DIFFERENT CRITERIA.` The clearest statement in the corpus that **a definitional change reaches backwards into evidence already collected**
span.quote: The Panel acknowledges that using these refined diagnostic criteria may change some of the outcomes of patients in natural history studies and clinical trials, when original expectations for outcomes may be based on subjects whose diagnosis was made using past, somewhat different criteria.

span.label: AND THE VALIDITY DOMAIN IS PRINTED TWICE, ONCE AT EACH END: `the McDonald Criteria SHOULD ONLY BE APPLIED IN THOSE PATIENTS WHO PRESENT WITH A TYPICAL CLINICALLY ISOLATED SYNDROME ... BECAUSE THE DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF THE CRITERIA HAVE BEEN LIMITED TO PATIENTS WITH SUCH PRESENTATIONS`, and in the Conclusions `THESE REVISED McDONALD CRITERIA ... SHOULD THEREFORE BE APPLIED ONLY WHEN PATIENTS HAVE EXPERIENCED A TYPICAL CIS`. A rule that states where it does not apply, twice
span.quote: In its discussions, the Panel stressed that the McDonald Criteria should only be applied in those patients who present with a typical clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) suggestive of MS or symptoms consistent with a CNS inflammatory demyelinating disease, because the development and validation of the Criteria have been limited to patients with such presentations. CIS presentations can be monofocal or multifocal, and typically involve the optic nerve, brainstem/cerebellum, spinal cord, or cerebral hemispheres.

span.label: AND AN INSTRUMENT MAY REPLACE THE OBSERVATION THE DEFINITION WAS BUILT ON: `Although the diagnosis can be made on clinical grounds alone, MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING ... CAN SUPPORT, SUPPLEMENT, OR EVEN REPLACE SOME CLINICAL CRITERIA ... The McDonald Criteria HAVE RESULTED IN EARLIER DIAGNOSIS OF MS with a high degree of both specificity and sensitivity, ALLOWING FOR BETTER COUNSELING OF PATIENTS AND EARLIER TREATMENT.` The scan does not merely support the clinical judgement - it stands in for it
span.quote: Although the diagnosis can be made on clinical grounds alone, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the central nervous system (CNS) can support, supplement, or even replace some clinical criteria, 3 – 9 as most recently emphasized by the so-called McDonald Criteria of the International Panel on Diagnosis of MS. 8 , 9 The McDonald Criteria have resulted in earlier diagnosis of MS with a high degree of both specificity and sensitivity, 10 – 13 allowing for better counseling of patients and earlier treatment.

span.label: AND `ATTACK` IS DEFINED WITH A DURATION FLOOR AND A CONFOUND EXCLUDED: `patient-reported symptoms or objectively observed signs typical of an acute inflammatory demyelinating event in the CNS, current or historical, WITH DURATION OF AT LEAST 24 HOURS, IN THE ABSENCE OF FEVER OR INFECTION ... Reports of paroxysmal symptoms should, however, CONSIST OF MULTIPLE EPISODES OCCURRING OVER NOT LESS THAN 24 HOURS.` A unit of disease activity given a minimum length, and a historical report admitted as evidence
span.quote: The Panel considered again what constitutes an attack (relapse, exacerbation) and defined this as patient-reported symptoms or objectively observed signs typical of an acute inflammatory demyelinating event in the CNS, current or historical, with duration of at least 24 hours, in the absence of fever or infection. Although a new attack should be documented by contemporaneous neurological examination, in the appropriate context, some historical events with symptoms and evolution characteristic for MS, but for which no objective neurological findings are documented, can provide reasonable evidence of a prior demyelinating event. Reports of paroxysmal symptoms (historical or current) should, however, consist of multiple episodes occurring over not less than 24 hours.

span.label: **AND A PHENOTYPE WAS SPLIT OFF PARTLY BECAUSE THE TREATMENT FAILS ON IT**: `There was agreement that THIS PHENOTYPE SHOULD BE SEPARATED FROM TYPICAL MS because of DIFFERENT CLINICAL COURSE, PROGNOSIS, AND UNDERLYING PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND POOR RESPONSE TO SOME AVAILABLE MS DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES.` Neuromyelitis optica leaves the class on four grounds, and one of them is that **the drugs for the parent class do not work**
span.quote: In its current review, the Panel focused specifically on the often-problematic differential diagnosis for MS of neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and NMO spectrum disorders. There is increasing evidence of relapsing CNS demyelinating disease characterized by involvement of optic nerves (unilateral or bilateral optic neuritis), often severe myelopathy with MRI evidence of longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions, often normal brain MRI (or with abnormalities atypical for MS), and serum aquaporin-4 (AQP4) autoantibodies. 16 , 17 There was agreement that this phenotype should be separated from typical MS because of different clinical course, prognosis, and underlying pathophysiology and poor response to some available MS disease-modifying therapies.

span.label: AND A TERM IS DIAGNOSED AS AN ADMIXTURE OF TWO OTHERS: `there is some uncertainty, especially in Asia, ABOUT WHETHER MS AND NMO ARE DISTINCT AND IF SO, HOW THEY SHOULD BE DISTINGUISHED. AS CURRENTLY APPLIED, THE TERM OPTICOSPINAL MS APPEARS TO BE AN ADMIXTURE OF CONVENTIONAL MS AND NMO.` A name in regional use that turns out to cover two classes the rest of the field separates
span.quote: Although the McDonald Criteria are widely used in these parts of the world, there is some uncertainty, especially in Asia, about whether MS and NMO are distinct and if so, how they should be distinguished. As currently applied, the term opticospinal MS appears to be an admixture of conventional MS and NMO.

span.label: AND THE TEST THAT SEPARATES THEM IS ASYMMETRIC: `ALTHOUGH NOT ALL PATIENTS WITH AN NMO-LIKE PRESENTATION WILL BE AQP4 ANTIBODY POSITIVE, THE MAJORITY ARE, WHEREAS THOSE WITH MS ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE AQP4 ANTIBODY NEGATIVE.` A marker that rules in better than it rules out, used to decide which disease a patient is treated for
span.quote: Although not all patients with an NMO-like presentation will be AQP4 antibody positive, the majority are, whereas those with MS are more likely to be AQP4 antibody negative.

span.label: AND THE IMAGING-ONLY CASE IS REFUSED A DIAGNOSIS: `occasional individuals investigated by MRI for indications unrelated to MS have INCIDENTAL FINDINGS of brain lesions with appearance and topography consistent with MS ... the Panel concluded that A FIRM DIAGNOSIS OF MS BASED ON INCIDENTAL FINDINGS ON MRI ALONE, EVEN WITH ADDITIONAL SUPPORTIVE FINDINGS ... IN THE ABSENCE OF MS-RELEVANT CLINICAL SYMPTOMS, IS PROBLEMATIC.` **The same images that can replace a clinical criterion cannot, alone, make the diagnosis** - a boundary drawn between supporting and constituting
span.quote: Many individuals with high lesion loads may have had a protracted subclinical disease course prior to their first clinical event. As a consequence, occasional individuals investigated by MRI for indications unrelated to MS have incidental findings of brain lesions with appearance and topography consistent with MS. Detection of this presymptomatic phase, or radiologically isolated syndrome, is increasingly common. Some of these individuals followed clinically and by serial imaging will develop DIT by MRI, and some have clinical disease-defining events after several years. 86 – 89 However, in the absence of supportive research findings, the Panel concluded that a firm diagnosis of MS based on incidental findings on MRI alone, even with additional supportive findings on evoked potentials or typical CSF findings in the absence of MS-relevant clinical symptoms, is problematic. A future definite diagnosis of MS, however, cannot be excluded and may be likely, depending on the evolution of neurologic symptoms and signs.

span.label: **THERE IS STILL NO CONFIRMATORY BIOMARKER**: `Although increased IgG index or the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF support an MS diagnosis, and AQP4 antibody assays can help in the differential diagnosis process, THERE ARE STILL NO SPECIFIC BIOMARKERS TO CONFIRM THE DIAGNOSIS.` Every criterion in this document is a proxy, and the document says so
span.quote: Although increased IgG index or the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF support an MS diagnosis, and AQP4 antibody assays can help in the differential diagnosis process, there are still no specific biomarkers to confirm the diagnosis. Several blood and CSF biomarkers may be promising, 62 – 65 and high-resolution spectral domain optical coherence tomography might be as good as VEP in assessing visual involvement. The diagnostic utility of such markers needs to be validated and tested prospectively.

span.label: AND THE CRITERIA ARE NOT VALIDATED IN THE POPULATIONS THE PAPER EXTENDS THEM TO: `These 2010 revisions ... ARE LIKELY TO BE APPLICABLE in pediatric, Asian, and Latin American populations ... The predictive validity of DIS and DIT based on a single first scan IN CHILDREN WITH CIS NEEDS TO BE CONFIRMED IN PROSPECTIVE STUDIES. THE McDONALD CRITERIA HAVE NOT YET BEEN VALIDATED IN ASIAN AND LATIN AMERICAN POPULATIONS.` **Extended and unvalidated in the same paragraph**, with `likely` carrying the weight
span.quote: These 2010 revisions to the McDonald Criteria are likely to be applicable in pediatric, Asian, and Latin American populations once careful evaluation for other potential explanations for the clinical presentation is made. The predictive validity of DIS and DIT based on a single first scan in children with CIS needs to be confirmed in prospective studies. The McDonald Criteria have not yet been validated in Asian and Latin American populations, and studies need to be done to confirm the sensitivity and specificity of the Criteria in such patients.

span.label: AND THE POPULATION THE RULE IS USED ON IS NOT THE ONE IT WAS TESTED ON: `A proportion of patients with nonspecific symptoms (eg, fatigue, weakness, or dizziness) and nonspecific MRI findings ARE REFERRED TO SECONDARY AND TERTIARY MS CENTERS ... FOR A SECOND OPINION AND DO NOT IN FACT HAVE MS`, and the Panel notes `only limited research and practical experience IN GENERAL NEUROLOGY PRACTICE POPULATIONS`. The criteria are validated in MS centres and applied in clinics
span.quote: A proportion of patients with nonspecific symptoms (eg, fatigue, weakness, or dizziness) and nonspecific MRI findings are referred to secondary and tertiary MS centers in the developed world for a second opinion and do not in fact have MS. These revised McDonald Criteria for MS diagnosis should therefore be applied only when patients have experienced a typical CIS (or progressive paraparesis/cerebellar/cognitive syndrome in the case of suspected PPMS).

span.label: AND AT LEAST ONE ATTACK MUST BE OBJECTIVELY CORROBORATED, WHICH IMPORTS THE INSTRUMENT INTO THE DEFINITION: `before a definite diagnosis of MS can be made, AT LEAST 1 ATTACK MUST BE CORROBORATED BY FINDINGS ON NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION, VISUAL EVOKED POTENTIAL RESPONSE ..., OR MRI CONSISTENT WITH DEMYELINATION IN THE AREA OF THE CNS IMPLICATED IN THE HISTORICAL REPORT.` A patient's history counts only where an instrument agrees with it
span.quote: There was consensus among the Panel members that before a definite diagnosis of MS can be made, at least 1 attack must be corroborated by findings on neurological examination, visual evoked potential (VEP) response in patients reporting prior visual disturbance, or MRI consistent with demyelination in the area of the CNS implicated in the historical report of neurological symptoms.

span.label: refusing to liberalise the MRI requirement for CSF-positive patients, because CSF status was not a variable in the studies the new imaging rule came from
span.note: eliminates: carrying an allowance from the old criteria into a rule set whose evidence base never tested it · outcome: held
span.quote: In the 2001 and 2005 McDonald Criteria, a positive CSF finding could be used to reduce the MRI requirements for reaching DIS criteria (requiring only 2 or more MRI-detected lesions consistent with MS if the CSF was positive). 8 , 9 However, when applying the simplified MAGNIMS imaging criteria for DIS and DIT, 24 the Panel believes that even further liberalizing MRI requirements in CSF-positive patients is not appropriate, as CSF status was not evaluated for its contribution to the MAGNIMS criteria for DIS and DIT.

span.label: restricting the criteria to patients presenting with a typical clinically isolated syndrome, stated in the Considerations and again in the Conclusions
span.note: eliminates: application to the nonspecific-symptom referrals who `DO NOT IN FACT HAVE MS` · outcome: partial
span.quote: In its discussions, the Panel stressed that the McDonald Criteria should only be applied in those patients who present with a typical clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) suggestive of MS or symptoms consistent with a CNS inflammatory demyelinating disease, because the development and validation of the Criteria have been limited to patients with such presentations. CIS presentations can be monofocal or multifocal, and typically involve the optic nerve, brainstem/cerebellum, spinal cord, or cerebral hemispheres.

span.label: requiring at least one attack to be corroborated by examination, evoked potentials or MRI in the implicated CNS area
span.note: eliminates: a diagnosis resting entirely on undocumented patient history · outcome: held
span.quote: There was consensus among the Panel members that before a definite diagnosis of MS can be made, at least 1 attack must be corroborated by findings on neurological examination, visual evoked potential (VEP) response in patients reporting prior visual disturbance, or MRI consistent with demyelination in the area of the CNS implicated in the historical report of neurological symptoms.

span.label: NMO
span.quote: In its current review, the Panel focused specifically on the often-problematic differential diagnosis for MS of neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and NMO spectrum disorders. There is increasing evidence of relapsing CNS demyelinating disease characterized by involvement of optic nerves (unilateral or bilateral optic neuritis), often severe myelopathy with MRI evidence of longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions, often normal brain MRI (or with abnormalities atypical for MS), and serum aquaporin-4 (AQP4) autoantibodies. 16 , 17 There was agreement that this phenotype should be separated from typical MS because of different clinical course, prognosis, and underlying pathophysiology and poor response to some available MS disease-modifying therapies.

span.label: typical MS
span.quote: In its current review, the Panel focused specifically on the often-problematic differential diagnosis for MS of neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and NMO spectrum disorders. There is increasing evidence of relapsing CNS demyelinating disease characterized by involvement of optic nerves (unilateral or bilateral optic neuritis), often severe myelopathy with MRI evidence of longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions, often normal brain MRI (or with abnormalities atypical for MS), and serum aquaporin-4 (AQP4) autoantibodies. 16 , 17 There was agreement that this phenotype should be separated from typical MS because of different clinical course, prognosis, and underlying pathophysiology and poor response to some available MS disease-modifying therapies.

span.label: opticospinal MS
span.quote: Although the McDonald Criteria are widely used in these parts of the world, there is some uncertainty, especially in Asia, about whether MS and NMO are distinct and if so, how they should be distinguished. As currently applied, the term opticospinal MS appears to be an admixture of conventional MS and NMO.

span.label: conventional MS
span.quote: Although the McDonald Criteria are widely used in these parts of the world, there is some uncertainty, especially in Asia, about whether MS and NMO are distinct and if so, how they should be distinguished. As currently applied, the term opticospinal MS appears to be an admixture of conventional MS and NMO.

span.label: The McDonald Criteria
span.quote: Although the diagnosis can be made on clinical grounds alone, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the central nervous system (CNS) can support, supplement, or even replace some clinical criteria, 3 – 9 as most recently emphasized by the so-called McDonald Criteria of the International Panel on Diagnosis of MS. 8 , 9 The McDonald Criteria have resulted in earlier diagnosis of MS with a high degree of both specificity and sensitivity, 10 – 13 allowing for better counseling of patients and earlier treatment.

span.label: earlier diagnosis of MS
span.quote: Although the diagnosis can be made on clinical grounds alone, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the central nervous system (CNS) can support, supplement, or even replace some clinical criteria, 3 – 9 as most recently emphasized by the so-called McDonald Criteria of the International Panel on Diagnosis of MS. 8 , 9 The McDonald Criteria have resulted in earlier diagnosis of MS with a high degree of both specificity and sensitivity, 10 – 13 allowing for better counseling of patients and earlier treatment.

span.label: a first MRI
span.quote: The 2005 revision of the McDonald Criteria simplified the MRI evidence required for DIT, basing it on the appearance of a new T2 lesion on a scan compared to a reference or baseline scan performed at least 30 days after the onset of the initial clinical event. In clinical practice, however, there is reason not to postpone a first MRI until after 30 days of clinical onset, which would result in an extra MRI scan to confirm a diagnosis. Abandoning the requirement for an extra reference MRI after 30 days does not compromise specificity, 28 and therefore the Panel, in its current revision of the McDonald Criteria, allows a new T2 lesion to establish DIT irrespective of the timing of the baseline MRI.

span.label: an extra MRI scan
span.quote: The 2005 revision of the McDonald Criteria simplified the MRI evidence required for DIT, basing it on the appearance of a new T2 lesion on a scan compared to a reference or baseline scan performed at least 30 days after the onset of the initial clinical event. In clinical practice, however, there is reason not to postpone a first MRI until after 30 days of clinical onset, which would result in an extra MRI scan to confirm a diagnosis. Abandoning the requirement for an extra reference MRI after 30 days does not compromise specificity, 28 and therefore the Panel, in its current revision of the McDonald Criteria, allows a new T2 lesion to establish DIT irrespective of the timing of the baseline MRI.

span.label: `attack` (relapse, exacerbation) - `patient-reported symptoms or objectively observed signs typical of an acute inflammatory demyelinating event in the CNS, current or historical, WITH DURATION OF AT LEAST 24 HOURS, IN THE ABSENCE OF FEVER OR INFECTION`
span.quote: The Panel considered again what constitutes an attack (relapse, exacerbation) and defined this as patient-reported symptoms or objectively observed signs typical of an acute inflammatory demyelinating event in the CNS, current or historical, with duration of at least 24 hours, in the absence of fever or infection. Although a new attack should be documented by contemporaneous neurological examination, in the appropriate context, some historical events with symptoms and evolution characteristic for MS, but for which no objective neurological findings are documented, can provide reasonable evidence of a prior demyelinating event. Reports of paroxysmal symptoms (historical or current) should, however, consist of multiple episodes occurring over not less than 24 hours.

span.label: `dissemination in time` (2010 sense) - satisfied EITHER by a new lesion on a later scan OR by enhancing and non-enhancing lesions coexisting on ONE baseline scan; the 2005 sense required a reference scan at least 30 days after onset
span.quote: The 2005 revision of the McDonald Criteria simplified the MRI evidence required for DIT, basing it on the appearance of a new T2 lesion on a scan compared to a reference or baseline scan performed at least 30 days after the onset of the initial clinical event. In clinical practice, however, there is reason not to postpone a first MRI until after 30 days of clinical onset, which would result in an extra MRI scan to confirm a diagnosis. span.label: `opticospinal MS` - a regionally used term that `APPEARS TO BE AN ADMIXTURE OF CONVENTIONAL MS AND NMO` rather than a class of its own
span.quote: Although the McDonald Criteria are widely used in these parts of the world, there is some uncertainty, especially in Asia, about whether MS and NMO are distinct and if so, how they should be distinguished. As currently applied, the term opticospinal MS appears to be an admixture of conventional MS and NMO.

span.label: `radiologically isolated syndrome` - MS-appearing lesions found incidentally, for which `A FIRM DIAGNOSIS OF MS BASED ON INCIDENTAL FINDINGS ON MRI ALONE ... IS PROBLEMATIC`; the imaging is present and the diagnosis is withheld
span.quote: Many individuals with high lesion loads may have had a protracted subclinical disease course prior to their first clinical event. As a consequence, occasional individuals investigated by MRI for indications unrelated to MS have incidental findings of brain lesions with appearance and topography consistent with MS. Detection of this presymptomatic phase, or radiologically isolated syndrome, is increasingly common. Some of these individuals followed clinically and by serial imaging will develop DIT by MRI, and some have clinical disease-defining events after several years. 86 – 89 However, in the absence of supportive research findings, the Panel concluded that a firm diagnosis of MS based on incidental findings on MRI alone, even with additional supportive findings on evoked potentials or typical CSF findings in the absence of MS-relevant clinical symptoms, is problematic. A future definite diagnosis of MS, however, cannot be excluded and may be likely, depending on the evolution of neurologic symptoms and signs.

span.label: extends → the original (2001) and revised (2005) McDonald Criteria, whose `UNDERLYING CONCEPTS ... ARE STILL VALID` and whose imaging requirements this revision replaces
span.quote: Since the revision of the McDonald Criteria in 2005, new data and consensus have pointed to the need for their simplification to improve their comprehension and utility and for evaluating their appropriateness in populations that differ from the largely Western Caucasian adult populations from which the Criteria were derived. In May 2010 in Dublin, Ireland, the International Panel on Diagnosis of MS (the Panel) met for a third time to examine requirements for demonstrating DIS and DIT and to focus on application of the McDonald Criteria in pediatric, Asian, and Latin American populations.

span.label: extends → the MAGNIMS network's comparison of the Barkhof/Tintore DIS criteria against Swanton's simplified criteria in 282 CIS patients, adopted here wholesale
span.quote: By using the recommended simplified MAGNIMS criteria to demonstrate DIS 22 and allowing DIT to be demonstrated by a scan containing both enhancing and nonenhancing lesions in regions of the CNS typical for MS, 23 a diagnosis of MS can be made in some CIS patients based on a single MRI. The Panel felt this is justified because it simplifies the diagnostic process without reducing accuracy. However, a new clinical event or serial imaging to show a new enhancing or T2 lesion will still be required to establish DIT in those patients who do not have both gadolinium-enhancing and nonenhancing lesions on their baseline MRI.

span.label: critiques → the term `opticospinal MS` as used in Asia, which `APPEARS TO BE AN ADMIXTURE OF CONVENTIONAL MS AND NMO`

As currently applied, the term opticospinal MS appears to be an admixture of conventional MS and NMO.

span.label: NMO —distinct-from→ typical MS
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — `There was agreement that THIS PHENOTYPE SHOULD BE SEPARATED FROM TYPICAL MS because of DIFFERENT CLINICAL COURSE, PROGNOSIS, AND UNDERLYING PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND POOR RESPONSE TO SOME AVAILABLE MS DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES.` **One of the four grounds is that the parent class's drugs do not work** - a boundary drawn partly by what happens when you treat across it, which is arain2010's treatment-response boundary in a different field
span.quote: In its current review, the Panel focused specifically on the often-problematic differential diagnosis for MS of neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and NMO spectrum disorders.
